subject_session: 6 sessions incl. sub-739783158/ses-760345702, sub-730760263/ses-755434585 (VISp, LGd/LP, CA1/DG)

headline_stat.name: fraction of responsive cortical units orientation-selective (drifting gratings)

stated_limitation: Two caveats are worth stating. Tuning widths are fit to only 8 sampled directions spaced 45 degrees apart, so widths below roughly 20 degrees are not resolvable and the reported median is best read as an upper bound on sharpness. And while the hippocampal control behaves as expected for drifting gratings, its static-grating rate is 19% (13 of 69 responsive units) rather than the nominal 5%. Permutation nulls that preserve slow drift (block shuffling) and short-lag correlations (circular shifts) did not remove that excess, so it is not explained by firing-rate nonstationarity.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000021 (Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels) with VISp, higher visual areas, visual thalamus, and a hippocampal negative control is exactly the standard choice for orientation selectivity.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile with explicit Allen QC criteria, correct trial windows for drifting vs static gratings, blank-trial baselines, and validated latency windows.
justification.analysis: Circular vector-strength gOSI with shuffle permutation nulls, cross-validated alignment, single-trial population decoding, and NeMoS GLMs, with a negative control that behaves as it should.
justification.correctness: Reported proportions, z-scores, decoding accuracies, and GLM pseudo-R2 gains are internally consistent with the figures and rest on sound, adequately powered statistics.
justification.figures: All nine figures clearly show the effect with labeled axes, units, and sample sizes, and example units span a range of selectivity rather than only the strongest.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate and the write-up volunteers specific limitations, including an anomaly (hippocampal static-grating false positives) that cuts against its own control.
justification.verdict: Sound, thorough, and honest end-to-end; I would accept the result and move on.
